Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-24
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (ArborPay CTO), Derek Mills (ArborPay SRE), Ana Suarez (ArborPay Head of Security)

Auto-generated Summary (may be incomplete):
ArborPay reported a cascade of credentialed fallthroughs across a subset of requests over the last 72 hours that increased tail latency and triggered SLA drops. Redwood SE walked through routing/fallback logic, proposed short-term routing policy to limit cross-region failovers, suggested circuit-breaker thresholds and KV/prefix cache validation steps. Action items agreed: share traces, run replay, schedule deep dive, confirm KMS/SSO constraints.

Topics:
- Incident timeline and scope
- Routing + fallback behavior (credentialed fallthrough)
- Impact on SLA and customer thresholds
- Short-term mitigations (policy changes, circuit-breaker tuning)
- Longer-term fixes (runtime patch, private deployment config, canary plan)

Action items (recorded above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, I know this is a follow up from the oncall thread, um we wanted to walk through the credentialed fallthroughs and map out a remediation path, we've got Liam from SE who dug into the traces 
[00:18] Priya: thanks, yeah it's been a rough 72 hours, um production latency spiked intermittently and a non trivial percent of requests fell through to the hosted fallback which then triggered downstream rate limits, that ended up taking out some user flows, so definitely high priority for us 
[00:35] Liam: right, quick context — the behavior we're calling "credentialed fallthrough" is where a token validation path fails in our routing layer for a subset of requests, routing policy then picks a compatible model variant in a remote region, the remote node returns slower and we hit tail latency — so it's a policy + routing edge case rather than the model itself 
[00:58] Derek: I'm trying to unpack why tokens that were valid earlier started failing, we suspect intermittent auth cache misses combined with a TTL expiry race, there was also a small config change to our SSO provider earlier this week, so could be correlated 
[01:15] Ana: security note — any change that causes fallthrough to hosted endpoints is a data residency concern for us, we need to keep PHI scoped to private or to the dedicated pool, remember that requirement.
[01:33] Samira: totally, Ana. that's why one of the things we'll cover is a short term routing policy to pin certain routes to dedicated capacity and also avoid cross-region remaps when credential checks are flaky 
[01:48] Priya: can you remind me how the fallback ordering works? I remember something about region preference then model variant compatibility but it's fuzzy 
[02:03] Liam: yeah so simplified — primary: same-region dedicated if available, then same-region hosted model family, then cross-region hosted fallbacks. we also have a per-tenant routing policy where you can opt into stricter locality or stricter cost. In ArborPay's case, your policy was slightly permissive to reduce cost, which allowed cross-region fallbacks during the auth miss window
[02:28] Priya: ok that matches our config, we did relax locality to save on egress. hindsight 
[02:36] Derek: quick note, during the incidents some requests were retried by our client library which made the downstream patterns worse because retries hit different routing outcomes, that added to the tail 
[02:50] Liam: yep, retries plus routing nondeterminism is a bad combo. one short term lever is to add a circuit breaker so that after X failed auth checks for a session we pin to local dedicated replicas or return a structured error to reduce retries 
[03:06] Samira: and we can also add a soft TTL bump for the auth cache on Redwood's side while you investigate the SSO change — basically increase grace window for token validation so brief auth provider flaps don't cause fallthroughs 
[03:22] Ana: would bumping TTL mean we keep sensitive tokens longer in cache? need to evaluate encryption at rest and KMS usage if we do that 
[03:33] Liam: good question — tokens are encrypted with customer KMS when on Private or Dedicated; in hosted we use per-tenant envelope keys. If you require HSM-backed KMS we can note that in the pilot.
[03:48] Priya: we might ask for that, yeah. for regulatory reasons. we'll confirm with compliance 
[03:55] Derek: we uploaded some trace files to the share, there's a couple request IDs where you can see the auth validation path and then the cross-region remap. I left notes in the file names but let me know if you need raw logs as well. link: https://files.redwood.internal/arbpay/traces/sep24 
[04:12] Samira: got it, Liam — can you talk through the immediate config change you recommend? and what risk that introduces? 
[04:21] Liam: immediate: 1) tighten routing policy for payment-related routes to prefer same-region dedicated nodes; 2) set per-session circuit-breaker threshold — after 3 failed auth validations in 30s, pin session to dedicated or fail fast with a structured 429-like response; 3) increase auth cache grace to 5s on Redwood side. Risk: slight increase in cost from more local dedicated usage, and if we pin sessions incorrectly there's a chance of uneven load distribution — but tuned limits should keep that small 
[04:48] Priya: cost is acceptable if we can avoid SLA breaches. what's the expected latency improvement? ballpark 
[04:56] Liam: from the sample traces we estimate a reduction of tail P99 from ~2.1s to ~500–700ms for affected flows when pinning to local dedicated; depends on model and input length but it's material 
[05:12] Ana: what about audit logging? we need end-to-end proof that requests never left region for the pilot 
[05:20] Samira: Redwood console provides per-request region tag and trace link, we can export an audit bundle. I'll include steps in the notes and share a doc: https://redwood.ai/docs/audit-bundle (placeholder) 
[05:33] Derek: we also want to run a controlled replay of traffic tilting auth failures so we can validate the circuit-breaker behavior before rolling widely. is there a harness you recommend? 
[05:42] Liam: yes, we have a replay harness that can inject auth-flap scenarios and exercise routing policies, it can be run against a staging replica or your dedicated pool. We'll send the harness and a runbook; it runs with minimal data retention and produces a short report 
[05:58] Priya: excellent. timeline — we can allocate SRE time to run the replay on Monday 2026-09-28, aim to share results by EOD 09-30 
[06:09] Samira: noted. Liam, followup — is there something in the runtime that needs a code patch or is this purely config/policy? 
[06:17] Liam: there's a small bug we've seen in the routing decision caching layer where credential validation failures weren't invalidating some cached decision shards quickly; we've got a candidate patch that forces cache invalidation on auth deltas — that will be a runtime patch (patch-1.2.3) and we should canary it in a dedicated pool first 
[06:36] Derek: timeline for patch? we prefer quick turnaround but want enough testing 
[06:41] Liam: we can push a hotfix branch and do an internal bake for 48 hours; with your permission we can canary to a small subset (5% of sessions) in your dedicated pool within 72 hours, then expand if metrics look good 
[06:56] Priya: yes let's do that, 5% canary sounds reasonable. we'll need rollback steps documented 
[07:02] Liam: absolutely — rollback is same-day and we've got automatic revert if error rates spike. we'll provide the runbook.
[07:10] Ana: conditional on KMS confirmation and audit requirements — we need the runbook and the SOC2 snippet before we greenlight the canary 
[07:18] Samira: I'll send our SOC2 summary and the KMS integration notes after the call.
[07:25] Priya: unrelated question — we noticed occasional spikes in memory usage on dedicated nodes during these windows, could that be related to the pinning you suggested?
[07:34] Liam: good catch — pinning can concentrate workload; that's why circuit-breaker thresholds plus a small local autoscale buffer are recommended. we can provision a temporary buffer for the pilot to avoid OOMs.
[07:46] Derek: we have alerts for memory > 75% that we can relax to 85% during the test window with ops oversight
[07:53] Samira: ok, Ops risk managed. next up: compliance and isolation — Ana what keys do you need to see to confirm HSM/KMS requirements?
[08:03] Ana: need a KMS architecture diagram, where envelope keys live, and proof of HSM-backed zone for the pilot. Also need RBAC audit trails for who can flip routing policies 
[08:15] Samira: noted, I'll attach both the diagram and the RBAC guide.
[08:20] Priya: any touchpoints with procurement or finance? we might need a short addendum to cover temporary dedicated usage and the canary costs 
[08:29] Samira: yes I'll include a draft pricing addendum for temporary dedicated buffer and canary. will cc finance.
[08:36] Derek: quick technical detail — the traces we uploaded show the auth lookup latency spiking to ~350ms for some calls, is that enough to cause TTL race?
[08:45] Liam: yes, if auth validation occasionally crosses the TTL boundary it can flip the cached decision; that's the race condition. patch ensures we invalidate decision shards on auth change events, which prevents the stale decision use 
[08:58] Priya: any risk to in-flight requests during the cache invalidation patch? like extra CPU or transient errors?
[09:06] Liam: minimal — we invalidate shards lazily and backfill; there may be a brief CPU blip under pathological conditions but we'll monitor during canary; rollback is immediate if we see any regressions
[09:19] Samira: ok wrapping towards next steps — we've got agreed actions to share traces, run replay, patch canary, and share compliance docs. anything else?
[09:29] Ana: please include an explicit list of endpoints that will be pinned for the pilot, with exact route names, so we can sign off on PD controls
[09:37] Liam: we'll send a proposed route list in the followup email — we'll default to payment-authorize/* and payment-capture/* as high priority
[09:46] Priya: schedule wise let's tentatively plan canary start 2026-09-29 with replay results before that, but SRE needs to confirm Monday availability 
[09:54] Derek: Monday confirmed for replay run here, we'll upload results by Thursday 9/30
[10:00] Samira: perfect. I'll create the shared checklist and post the links in chat, including a short runbook link: https://redwood.ai/internal/runbooks/canary-auth-fix (placeholder)
[10:12] Priya: thanks Samira, we've also looped in our compliance engineer so they can review the SOC docs when you share them
[10:20] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the 2-hour deep dive; any final questions?
[10:28] Priya: none from me, thanks 
[10:31] Derek: no, thanks 
[10:33] Ana: thanks all, please add me to the shared folder for the artifacts
[10:36] Samira: will do. end of call.
